idiom_name: Pekko IO(Tcp) Bind/Connect + Register; Pekko Streams Tcp.bind/outgoingConnection
implementation_notes: Pekko classic TCP internalises establishment behind a manager acquired with IO(Tcp): Bind is the acceptor command, Connect is the connector command, and after Connected the peer registers a per-connection handler actor. In Pekko Streams, Tcp(system).bind(host, port) returns a Source[IncomingConnection, Future[ServerBinding]] and outgoingConnection is the connector-side Flow, with stream back-pressure. Pull-mode classic acceptance requires ResumeAccepting after each Connected; failure to do so stalls the listener.
pitfalls: In pull mode the listener must receive ResumeAccepting or acceptance stalls.
Register must arrive before the connection actor's internal timeout or the connection is silently closed.
Actor-per-connection without stream back-pressure buffers without bound; use Flow.withAttributes(Attributes) to cap buffer sizes.
Bound the connection actor system mailbox size; overflow causes head-of-line blocking on the listener.
Acquire the classic manager with IO(Tcp); it is an actor reference, not a separately started server. Send Bind or Connect and handle CommandFailed/Connected before registering the handler.
